controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body colour at its measured dayside temperature, 1,499 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The colour of HD 209458 b's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 4.5 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

controls.label: Spitzer
controls.qualification: Published fit · Zellem et al. 2014 · Spitzer 4.5 µm, 2010 · longitude only
controls.notes: Brightness temperature at 4.5 µm from Zellem et al. (2014)'s published fit to a Spitzer phase curve of January 2010. Their one sinusoid becomes a map of longitude through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion, so there is no north-south detail and every latitude is drawn alike. The hottest longitude is 41° east of noon. The false colour runs from 850 to 1,600 K. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.
